newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Clash in south Albania, opposition appeals to West.
newsitem.headline: Clash in south Albania, opposition appeals to West.

text.p: Government troops fought armed insurgents in southern Albania on Wednesday as opposition politicians urged the West to put pressure on President Sali Berisha to help end the crisis.

In the first major clash after three days of emergency rule, the Albanian army pulled back from fierce fighting near a village to the east of the Adriatic port of Sarande, eyewitnesses said. Four villagers and at least two soldiers were reported wounded in exchanges that lasted about 40 minutes.
"The people won. The army, about 60 soldiers, got in their trucks and drove away," Sarande's former prefect Dimitris Stefos told Reuters in Athens by telephone.
Opposition parties appealed to the United States and Europe to exert influence to force Berisha government to the table.

The 11-party Forum for Democracy, grouped around the Socialists, the successor to the communist party, said it wanted an end to emergency rule and called for the West to link financial aid to political reform.
"Being convinced that the crisis has a political solution, we appeal to them to do their best to avoid a civil war in Albania," the group said in a statement.
Berisha on Tuesday rejected the opposition's call for government of "technocrats". He rejected any coalition grouping his ruling Democratic Party and the opposition Socialists.
The president issued no fresh political initiatives on Wednesday, but suggested an overnight curfew be shortened by three hours in Tirana and other areas unaffected by unrest.
Authorities announced that army chief of staff General Sheme Kosova had been dismissed and replaced by Major General Adem Copani, Berisha's personal military adviser.

A statement from the prime minister's office published in the newspaper Rilindja Demokratike said Kosova had been sacked for failing to ensure adequate security at military posts stormed and looted of their weapons by "terrorists".

The international community issued fresh expressions of concern about the crisis. Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok told reporters in Paris the European Union was sending his country's foreign minister to Albania on Friday for emergency talks.
A mission of the Council of Europe, the Strasbourg-based body overseeing human rights throughout the continent, was arriving in Tirana on Wednesday.
The delegation planned to meet Berisha and seek contact with all political forces during its two-day visit.
Albanian troops have been pressing south from the capital Tirana since Monday to reinstate government authority in the region, which erupted in violence at the weekend.
Government officials said the army, backed by police, had secured roads to the flashpoint of Vlore on the Adriatic coast and the mountainous route between the inland town of Gjirokaster and Sarande.
In Vlore, two people were killed and 19 injured in gunfire, the Health Ministry said. Over 20 people are reported to have died in the town since fresh violence erupted there last Friday.
Albania said on Wednesday that army chief of staff General Sheme Kosova had been dismissed and replaced by Major General Adem Copani, President Sali Berisha's personal military adviser.
A Defence Ministry statement said Kosova had been replaced by Copani. Neither said whether Kosova had been arrested.
